title: Instagram
summary: Photo and video sharing at billions-of-users scale: direct-to-storage media uploads with async processing, a ranked feed built from a hybrid fan-out, Stories with 24-hour expiry, and sharded Postgres/Cassandra behind aggressive caching.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Upload photos/videos with captions; follow users; like and comment
Home feed (ranked), profile grid, Stories (expire after 24 h), Explore
Feed loads < 500 ms; media appears instantly for the uploader
2B+ monthly users; heavy read skew; celebrity accounts with 600M followers

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Media storage and delivery dominate: 200 TB a day of originals plus renditions, served through a CDN. The database side is sharded metadata and a precomputed feed.

head: Data
Key
Store
rows: IDs embed logical shard (Instagram ID: 41 bits ms | 13 bits shard | 10 bits seq)
Sharded Postgres (thousands of logical shards on fewer hosts)

blocks.text: Instagram's engineering blog describes generating IDs inside Postgres with PL/pgSQL so the shard is encoded in the ID — any service can route by ID without a lookup.

blocks.caption: Media goes straight to storage; metadata and feed go through services

items: App gets a presigned URL, uploads the original straight to object storage, and shows it locally right away.
Storage event → processing creates sizes (150 px thumbnail up to 1080 px) and video renditions; CDN serves them.
App creates the post with the media ID; post service writes metadata and publishes PostCreated.
Fan-out workers push post IDs into followers' feed caches (skip celebrities and inactive users).
Feed read: cached IDs + celebrity pulls → ranking → hydrate → return.
Candidates: followed accounts' recent posts (pushed + pulled), plus suggested posts.
Ranking model predicts p(like), p(comment), p(save), p(time spent); score = weighted sum; then diversity rules (no 5 posts in a row from one author).
Precompute feeds for users likely to open the app soon; compute lazily for others.
Seen-state: keep a bloom filter / recent set per user to avoid repeats.
Separate pipeline from feed: stories expire after 24 h, so storage uses TTL (Cassandra TTL, object lifecycle rules).
Story tray = ranked list of followed users with active stories; cache per user, invalidate on new story by followees (fan-out of a 'has new story' marker, not content).
Prefetch the first story's media for the top tray entries for instant playback.
Seen markers per (viewer, story) written async; viewer lists for authors read from Cassandra.
Write the like (post_id, user_id) idempotently; increment counters asynchronously.
Hot posts: sharded counters or batched increments (aggregate in memory for 1 s, then write).
Show approximate counts ("1.2M likes"); exact for small numbers.
Notifications: like events → aggregation ('Alice and 20 others liked your photo') → push.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Pull path for celebrities, sharded counters, cache replicas
Uploader sees local copy; prioritize small sizes; autoscale workers
Move logical shards to new hosts; read replicas; cache
CDN miss storm on viral media
Origin shield, pre-warm after posting for big accounts

items.title: Non-functional
items.text: Fast feed, instant upload feel, celebrity skew.

items.title: API + data
items.text: Presigned upload, ID with shard bits.

items.title: HLD
items.text: Storage + processing; post service; fan-out; feed cache.

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Celebrity handling, CDN metrics, processing lag.

items.a: Embedding-based candidate retrieval from accounts/posts similar to what you engage with, then a ranking model; heavily cached.

items.q: How do you delete a post everywhere?
items.a: Tombstone in metadata; feeds filter at hydration; CDN purge for media; async cleanup.
Separate messaging system (like WhatsApp/Slack design): per-conversation partitions, WebSocket/MQTT delivery.

items: Presigned direct uploads; async resize/transcode; CDN delivery.
IDs encode logical shard → routing without lookup.
Hybrid fan-out; celebrities pulled at read.
Stories = TTL storage + tray cache.
Likes written idempotently, counted async.
